financing.summary: KB Home (NYSE: KBH; FY ends Nov 30) finances land on its own balance sheet: in June 2025 its then-CFO said it uses 'extremely limited land banking or other off-balance sheet vehicles', and no land-bank counterparty is named in any 2025-2026 filing or release. At Aug 31, 2026 it owned or controlled 61,581 lots (37,129 owned, 24,452 optioned, ~40% optioned, down from 49% optioned at FY2024) after walking away from 24,596 controlled lots in FY2025 and 8,777 more in the first nine months of FY2026. Funding is a $1.2B unsecured revolver (Bank of America agent, due Nov 2030; $415M drawn at Q3 FY2026), a $360M unsecured term loan (Wells Fargo agent, due Nov 2029) and four unsecured note series totalling $1.34B, with the next maturity the $300M 6.875% notes due June 15, 2027; liquidity fell to $942M and debt-to-capital rose to 35.7% (net of cash ~33.9%, derived) versus a stated ~30% target, while buybacks continued ($175M in 9M FY2026). Room for a land banker: owned-lot share is ~60% and rising, leverage is above target with a 2027 maturity ahead, and the land chief (EVP Real Estate & Business Development Albert Praw) retires Nov 30, 2026 with the CFO seat filled only on an interim basis by the CEO since May 2026, so land-finance relationships are in transition.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, balance-sheet funded. 10-K: seeks to own or control land for the next three to five years of forecast production and a one- to three-year supply per product line per community; typically ties land up with small option payments or earnest-money deposits at pre-set prices, develops in smaller phases, assets generally 50-250 lots, and may sell or monetize land. Optioned share fell from 49% (Nov 2024) to 43% (Nov 2025) to 40% (Aug 2026) as KB cancelled options that no longer met underwriting. Management (Q2 2025 call) framed balance-sheet land funding with 'extremely limited land banking' as a transparency and cost advantage. Remaining purchase price on all option contracts at Aug 31, 2026: $358.3M (rest of 2026), $859.0M (2027), $297.3M (2028), $98.5M (2029), $4.0M (2030). Land spend (land + development + fees) was $2.84B FY2024, $2.61B FY2025, $1.79B in 9M FY2026 (West Coast 47%); West Coast holds $3.21B of the $5.98B inventory. Entered Atlanta organically in May 2026 (110 homesites).

lots.note: Owned/optioned from the deck's lot-position chart; total and 'approximately 60% owned / 40% under contract' confirmed in the Q3 FY2026 press release and 10-Q MD&A. By segment (total lots, 10-Q): West Coast 20,471; Southwest 10,165; Central 18,967; Southeast 11,978. 9,549 of the optioned lots carry deposits refundable at KB's discretion. Prior points: Nov 30, 2025 64,612 (37,137 owned / 27,475 optioned; segment split WC 20,750, SW 11,142, Central 20,614, SE 12,106 per FY2025 10-K); Nov 30, 2024 76,703 (51% owned). years_supply is derived (not company-stated): 61,581 lots / 11,116 trailing-12-month deliveries (3,619 in Q4 FY2025 + 7,497 in 9M FY2026).

land_banking.description: Option contracts where a third-party land financier or developer buys a parcel on KB's behalf (or a landowner improves it) and KB is effectively compelled to exercise; KB books the land and a matching financing liability. Liability was $11.0M at Aug 31, 2026 vs $15.4M at Nov 30, 2025, which shows land banking is very small at KB.
